hook: One number put a mother behind bars.

instagram.caption:
One number put a mother behind bars.

Sally Clark lost two infant sons. A paediatrician squared a single base rate and told the jury the odds were 1 in 73 million.

The Royal Statistical Society wrote to the courts and said the number was wrong — two probabilities only multiply cleanly when events are independent. In this family, they were not.

Her conviction was overturned in 2003. She died four years later.

Save this — and question the numbers.
